newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia asks for death sentence in U.S. slayings.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia asks for death sentence in U.S. slayings.

text.p: State prosecutors have asked a Jakarta court to hand down a death sentence on an Indonesian man accused of murdering three people in the United States, the official Antara news agency reported on Wednesday.

Chief Prosecutor Kamaru said he believed he had proved to the panel of three judges that Harnoko Dewantono, also known as Oki, had killed two Indonesians and an Indian national in Los Angeles in 1991 and 1992.
"The defendant has been found to have deliberately planned their murders," Kamaru was quoted as telling the court on Tuesday.
Kamaru said Dewantono had killed his Indian business partner Suresh Mirchandani in August 1991.
"Suresh died of a bullet wound in his chest. His body was wrapped in a plastic bag after the hands were chopped off," the prosecutor was quoted as telling the Central Jakarta State Court.
Dewantono's Indonesian school friend, Gina Sutan Awar, and his brother, Erry Prihanto, both died after being hit on the head with blunt objects also in Los Angeles in 1992, he added.
Los Angeles police unsuccessfully sought the extradition of Dewantono, a former U.S. resident, after the three bodies were found together in a leased storage locker in August 1994.
Dewantono had by then returned to Indonesia, where he was arrested and tried.
The defence wraps up its arguments on April 15 and a verdict will be pronounced a few weeks later.
